tasks.title: Wait and Resume
tasks.objective: Represent delays with resume deadlines and retain an in-memory execution cursor, without sleeping a worker for the entire wait.
acceptance_criteria: Early resume does not advance incorrectly.
Eligible resume continues from the correct step without replaying earlier completed actions in the tested in-memory scenario.
No durable restart guarantee is claimed.

evidence.result: Acceptance criterion 1: PrepareWait() validates the workflow configuration and WAIT identity/type, snapshots the configured step map and calculates ResumeAt once using now.Add(step.Delay). Early resume attempts return ErrWaitNotReady without changing cursor, deadline or consumption and without executing downstream callbacks (TestWaitPreparationAndEarlyResume). Acceptance criterion 2: exact-deadline and later attempts are eligible; ResumeWait() consumes before callbacks and starts at the saved WAIT successor through existing ExecuteActions() sequential continuation. Previously completed actions are not replayed in the tested sequential scenario; consumed waits return ErrWaitConsumed without replay. Terminal, condition and subsequent WAIT handoffs are supported. Downstream action failures preserve the failed cursor and underlying error (TestWaitResumeWithoutReplay, TestWaitResumeBoundaries, TestWaitFailureConsumesWithoutRetry). Acceptance criterion 3: WaitState is in-memory/process-local only; no durable persistence, scheduler or restart recovery exists. Passing tests establish local behavior, not production durability. Additional tests: TestWaitRejectsInvalidInput and TestWaitDefinitionSnapshot. Six test functions and 11 subtests. Historical implementation evidence, recorded in committed PROGRESS.md and docs/HANDOFF.md and the supplied implementation report: explicit human authorization preceded implementation; RED compilation failed because the new wait/resume API was undefined; GREEN tests passed after implementation. Prior permission-enabled full verification passed tracker validation, 44 Python harness tests, Go unit tests, Go race tests, go vet and both Git whitespace checks. Sandbox Go-cache denials were environmental failures, not intentional RED results. The documentation session separately recorded an initial sandbox Go-cache denial followed by permission-enabled full verification PASS. These historical checks are not newly executed RED/GREEN tests; no pre-activation preflight was rerun. Published implementation commit: 10a270486f5df4b591852db90b6264b5e6d5ab2c. Published documentation commit: 9c57598597a1d081cc6fbc60da1c683a976a3478. Fresh acceptance startup (2026-11-12): clean main at the documentation commit; initialization and tracker validation passed. Live GitHub main was independently resolved through the GitHub connector to 9c57598597a1d081cc6fbc60da1c683a976a3478, separate from cached origin/main. Limitations: state is process-local, not durable; no background scheduler or polling. WaitState requires single-caller access, must not be copied and does not support concurrent ResumeWait() or Snapshot() access. Definitions must not be mutated concurrently with PrepareWait(). Repeated PrepareWait() calls create independent states; preparation validates configuration, not prior execution provenance. Consuming before callbacks prevents ordinary sequential replay but does not guarantee exactly-once external effects. Failure after consumption requires separately designed reconciliation or recovery. Callback panics are not recovered and may leave an imprecise saved cursor. No callback cancellation or timeout was introduced. Handler registrations and captured callback inputs are not snapshotted; registry concurrency constraints still apply. No M2 lifecycle integration exists yet. No production deployment, measured business outcome or distributed correctness guarantee is claimed.
